lens: Brand guardian and truth. All 12 posts of each V3 proposal were read in full (concept, cover, layers, storyboard, slides, end card, caption, first comment, alt text, claims check), against BRIEF.md, BRIEF-V3.md, the owner-taste syntheses in the three artifacts files, brand-bible.md (claim table, never-list, copy bank) and options A and B as selected. Prices and stock were checked by script against research/roster.json: every quoted price and variant count in all four proposals is correct, nothing is pre-order or under 10; the thinnest heroes are North Star Bangle 10/10 (Galli P4, Drawn From Life P2), Petal Flower Studs 10/10 (Galli P11) and Droplet Open Cuff 10/10 (Niwas P4), and Ruby bracelet/huggies at 12. Listing facts (mm, cm, g, closures, plating, 'slips over the hand', 'two endings', 'set of two', care lines, Toggle 12 g) were checked against src/data/jewellerySnapshot.ts and all hold; store hours (Mon-Sat 10-7) and the WhatsApp number were checked in the site code. Kit check: Velista DOES carry È (so 'PRISM RIVIERE' can stay in Velista) and lacks the rupee sign, middot and degree sign. Caption scan: no em dashes, exclamation marks or emoji in any caption or first comment; every hook is 122 characters or less; every first comment carries 5 tags; every caption ends on the bracket kicker. Viewed: the PTAT reference, the live grid, the motion COOKBOOK and both demo strips, the cut-out sheet, and the Box Theatre prototype cover (work/v3box/proto/p2-full.png). Ten criteria, 1-10 each: (1) brand fit, (2) owner-taste fit, (3) price and stock truth, (4) claim and wording truth (gold, emerald, rhodium, tags, care, scale), (5) cultural accuracy and spellings, (6) premium vs kitsch risk incl. reads-AI-made, (7) restraint, (8) caption quality and rules, (9) wordmark and type rules, (10) originality against A and B (V3 must not re-skin them).

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-free.json · NAIRA NIWAS (one building, one window a post)
scores.criteria: brand fit 8: a blush Bombay-Deco building in the Naira box's own colour, the I-flower as the kandil's light, the end-card flower turning at the owner's 10 s, real pieces at true relative scale inside each window; but it invents a second name ('NAIRA NIWAS') and sets it in type on 11 covers. | owner-taste fit 8: present-day housing-society wit told with love (watchman, 'kahi nako', the borrowed necklace, LOST: ONE EARRING), her own approved lines ('still lit.', 'Tied the knot. With myself.'), lilac/plum nights, one prop and one piece per window, true scale stated in px/mm, motion at her numbers; against it: blush plaster on every tile, a second Indian cue (kandil) on P2 and P6, the box's black velvet bed visible on P3 and P7. | price and stock 9: all correct, guards per post, and the finale moved to the green set (20/16/15) instead of Ruby at 12. | wording truth 7: careful listing words throughout (Silk Mesh 2.5 cm opening, Droplet 'two endings', Marquise 'sold as a set of two, never a choker', Baroque's no-water care line), but 'emerald-green' on P9 and P12 image text, 'made to stay gold.' in the Dhanteras and Diwali captions, and 'LISTED AS TARNISH FREE.' at 80 px on P5's end card. | cultural 9: ovalni and 'काही नको.' on Padwa, panatis, akash kandil to Tripurari Purnima, bangle-wala soap, tamarind and lemon on the brass, Kartik moon; four short Marathi strings all correct. | premium vs kitsch 7: the Deco elevation can be elegant, but 18 AI plates include photographic props (soap dish, vati, panatis, glasses, mirror, dupattas, silk) sitting right beside real pieces, so any AI tell lands next to the product. | restraint 7: a strict per-window budget, but every cover still carries facade grooves + kandil + headline + turn + prop + piece + plate. | captions 9: the best set ('Back in five minutes, said the card on the counter. It was eleven weeks.', 'He believed her.'), exact offer line in 7 of 12, COD and shipping lines, no dashes. | wordmark/type 6: real wordmark only on end cards and the P12 crown, but typed 'NAIRA PETITE' at 104 px (P1 fascia), 'NAIRA NIWAS' on every plate and P3's board, and P12 stacks the real wordmark with typed 'NIWAS' and निवास (a modified lockup). | originality 8: a new lane neither A nor B touches, new piece-moment pairings (Droplet cuff for Bhaubeej, Kiss Knot for Padwa, Marquise borrowed, Baroque under the moon); shares the Ruby opener and A's kandil as a device.
best_posts: P7 'काही नको. AND HE BELIEVED HER. (so she tied the knot herself.)': Padwa told in perfect Marathi as a self-purchase; Kiss Knot 20/20, listing tip 'wear both, knots on top' builds BUY2; reuses her approved 'Tied the knot. With myself.'
P9 'LOST: ONE EARRING.': the society notice is the headline object; Baguette Huggies' hinged snap and the listing's own 'mismatch them' tip; claims check correctly avoids 'you won't lose it'.
P8 'TWO NECKLACES. (the neighbour will ask for one.)': the joke is a product fact (Marquise Layering Set, sold as a set of two), 'or get her her own' is a natural BUY2; 40 in stock, 1 sold.
P4 'WINDOW SEAT: STILL DISPUTED.': the Droplet Open Cuff's listing line ('two endings ... sitting across a small gap') becomes a chalk line no sibling crosses; posted 8 days before Bhaubeej.

P11 'THE MOON IS BACK. (nobody's fasting this time.)': the season's calm tile, with the Baroque Shell's honest care line quoted (out of the shower, the pool and the sea), the kind of correction the owner rates highest.
weakest_posts: P12 crown: real wordmark + typed 'NIWAS' + निवास in one lockup, 'THE EMERALD-GREEN SET' as the end-card head, 26 strands of lights over a dense corner; the finale reads busier than the season.

P5 'TAMARIND AND LEMON': a kitchen-metal still life (the owner retired kitchen still lifes), 'LISTED AS TARNISH FREE.' promoted to an 80 px image headline, and 'made to stay gold.' on Dhanteras, the gold-buying day.
P3 'THE WATCHMAN KNOWS': typed 'NAIRA NIWAS CO-OPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY' board, the black velvet bed showing in the open drawer, 7 slides.
P2 'NO SOAP REQUIRED': strong joke, but the bangle wall + soap dish + kandil + Devanagari board make two Indian cues on one tile.
must_fix: Typed brand name: replace 'NAIRA PETITE' (P1 fascia) and the 'NAIRA NIWAS' line on every plate and on P3's board with the kit wordmark or drop NAIRA from them (the plate can read 'SHOP 1 / FLAT 103'); on P12 the crown carries the kit wordmark alone, no typed 'NIWAS' joined to it. The owner must approve 'Naira Niwas' as a season name before any of it is drawn (the Reissue's invented sub-brand was a must-fix).

'emerald-green' on P9 (end card, caption, first comment) and P12 (headline 'THE EMERALD-GREEN SET', end card, caption, alt text): write 'green' / 'green cubic zirconia' ('THE GREEN SET'); the house line 'EMERALD GREEN, not emerald.' is only safe with its correction.
'made to stay gold.' appears in the P5 Dhanteras and P6 Diwali captions: on the category's gold-buying days it reads as a gold-content wink; keep it only on P12 or set it with the tone bracket.
P5 end card: move 'LISTED AS TARNISH FREE.' (tagged, but a care claim as an 80 px headline) into the caption, where it already sits.

AI props next to real pieces (soap dish AI-07, vati AI-11, panatis AI-13, reading glasses AI-14, mirror AI-16, dupattas AI-18, silk AI-19, counter tray AI-05): check each at 100% beside the cut-out; any that reads generated falls back to flat SVG as the proposal says.
Black velvet bed of the real box shows on P3 and P7 (the owner's 'never black'): crop tight to the piece or keep the drawer three-quarter so only a sliver of bed shows.
Droplet Open Cuff is 10 Gold / 10 Silver (P4): re-read the evening of 2 Nov; Marathi reader for बांगड्या, शुभ दीपावली, काही नको., निवास.
graftable: P7 'काही नको. AND HE BELIEVED HER.' as the Padwa post in any option.
P9 'LOST: ONE EARRING.' society notice as a headline object.
P8 'TWO NECKLACES. the neighbour will ask for one.' for the Marquise set.
P11's quoted Baroque Shell care line as the house's honest pearl note.
The green set as the finale, so the top-left tile does not depend on Ruby at 12.
The true-relative-scale rule with a stated px/mm per frame, and the end-card wordmark flower turning at 36 degrees a second.

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-illustrated-films.json · DRAWN FROM LIFE (twelve small films)
scores.criteria: brand fit 8: the brand deck's peach-tulip and sage watercolour as washes, Lilac-mast ink, the real wordmark as the artist's signature on every cover, and a thesis that is the owner's own positioning ('the moment goes. the piece stays.' = 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.'); sketching was one of the account's two breakout topics. | owner-taste fit 7: quiet, one drawing, one piece, true scale on bodies, body fragments never faces, lilac and night papers; but two of her explicit rejections sit in its core technique: 'the line work just fought the picture' (graphic line over photographs) and 'anything that reads AI-made' (12 AI line plates of hands, ears, napes, palms), plus food she dropped (chakli, pedha, rice). | price and stock 8: all correct, swap rules per post; North Star 10/10 on P2, Ruby on P4 and P12. | wording truth 9: the most careful of the four: 'gold tone', 'rhodium coated', 'green cubic zirconia', 'ruby-red, clear, green or purple', 'joined by small stacked gold-tone rings' (A's own must-fix), 'shown larger.' on objects, 'listed as tarnish free' only on the tagged chain; one wink to fix ('still on at breakfast'). | cultural 9: chalni and lota, faral in steel, aukshan with kumkum, Padwa gift, brass polishing, mehendi, pinned pleats, 2 a.m. jhumkas; only आई and शुभ विवाह in Devanagari, both correct. | premium vs kitsch 7: fine-line ink and watercolour is the most luxury register of the four (Hermès-style), but AI anatomy is the hardest thing to make read real. | restraint 8: one drawing, one piece, one headline, one signed margin; flipbooks P3 and P9 run fuller; the hidden flower cameo is a gimmick. | captions 9: 'We went quiet for eleven weeks. We were drawing.', 'R.S.V.P. Nobody does. Everybody comes.', 'The heavy ones come off at 2 a.m.'; offer line in 4 of 12. | wordmark/type 9: kit wordmark once per frame on every cover, three brand faces + two Devanagari words, no typed brand name; the flower cameo bends the ghost rule (optional). | originality 3: the look is new, the content is not: P2 is A's 'THE MOON IS ALWAYS LATE', P3 is B's dabba-and-chakli joke, P6 is B's Prism-on-rangoli, P7 is A P3's 'kisne diya? maine.', P9 is A's grafted neckline guide with nearly the same lengths and pieces, P12 is A and B's Ruby set, P4 reuses A's 'send to your brother' format.
best_posts: P12 'THE HEAVY ONES COME OFF AT 2 A.M. (the huggies stay.)': the season's thesis as a scene, the Ruby set basket at list price, and a storyboard of all twelve films as the last slide.
P11 'NOBODY SEES THE SAFETY PINS. (everybody sees the bracelet.)': steel and brass pins rhyme with the Duo Link's two metals; listing words exact; ₹999, 20 in stock, 0 sold.
P8 'R.S.V.P. (nobody does. everybody comes.)': the card's linked-rings monogram becomes the Bold Nocturne Drops (a link hanging from a link); sends-driven and true.
P10 'MEHENDI'S DRYING. (so someone else put these on.)': the dots-to-a-drop motif is literally the Mint Pear Drop; tag-the-cousin prompt.
P4 'RED, LIKE THE TILAK. (consider this a hint.)': aukshan drawn correctly, kumkum-to-ruby-red as the anaar mechanism in motion, 8 days before Bhaubeej.
weakest_posts: P2 'THE MOON IS LATE.': option A's P2 headline almost word for word, and framed as 'every terrace in north India' for a buyer who is 46% Maharashtra.
P3 'THIS YEAR'S FARAL. (it'll outlast the chakli.)': option B's P6 joke ('it came with chakli') in a tiffin; chakli is on the owner's dropped-food list and the kicker adds 'no chakli was harmed'.
P9 'GALA KAISA CHAHIYE?': option A's grafted neckline guide (36 cm Baguette, 40 cm Serpentine, 45/50 cm, Toggle) re-drawn; the couture insight is A's spine.
P6 'A RANGOLI LASTS ONE NIGHT.': option B's P5 pairing (Prism Rivière on a rangoli) again.
must_fix: Re-angle the posts that repeat A or B before V3 is shown beside them: P2 (A's moon-late headline), P3 (B's dabba/chakli), P6 (B's Prism rangoli), P7 ('kisne diya? maine.' is A P3's line), P9 (A's neckline guide), P12 (A and B both close on the Ruby set; use Crystal or green).

AI anatomy: 12 of 18 plates (PL-07 to PL-18) are generated line drawings of hands, ears, napes, palms and a saree waist. Build P1 first, show the owner the plate at 100%, and keep the agent-drawn single-line fallback ready for every plate with a finger problem.
Owner's 'the line work fought the picture': keep the 14 px paper halo absolute and washes at 45% or less, so no line or wash ever crosses a piece.
Food the owner dropped: remove the drawn pedha and rice grains (P4), the 'chakli, in bulk' first comment (P7) and the 'no chakli was harmed' kicker (P3).
P12 kicker 'still on at breakfast' implies sleeping in the huggies, which no care note covers: change to 'still on at the next function'.
Flower cameo hidden in every film: off by default (it bends the 6-15% ghost rule); the owner may switch it on.
Confirm the 36 cm Baguette Tennis Necklace length on the PDP (it comes from alt text) before P9 and P12; Marathi/Hindi reader for आई and शुभ विवाह.
graftable: The sign-off 'the moment goes. the piece stays.' as a season line in any option.
The rhyme as a match-dissolve: one drawn everyday shape becomes the photographed piece in exactly its footprint ('Anaar, pre-peeled.' in motion).
The 14 px paper halo rule: the pen never touches the piece; true scale on a body, 'shown larger.' on objects.
The signed margin: N° 07/12, a pencil-italic inscription, the kit wordmark as the signature, same place on every cover.
P11 safety pins, P8 R.S.V.P. and P12 2 a.m. jhumkas as wedding-season scenes; P10 mehendi for drop earrings.

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-galli.json · NAIRA GALLI (twelve shops on one lane)
scores.criteria: brand fit 7: house palette, Velista/Cormorant/Jost, real cut-outs only, the kit wordmark on P1's board and every end card; but the lane is a generic Indian nostalgia device (a 'Wes Anderson' / 'Grand Budapest' pastiche in its own words), not Naira's own story, and it adds a typed sub-brand. | owner-taste fit 6: the Indian everyday-object wit she loves (bangle-wala soap, money order, bartan bhandar, the ladi she approved as plate 67 with this very bracelet, the optician, the bank pen), but the densest drawn world of the four: drawn bangles, jars of sweets, steel shelves, flower baskets, umbrellas, diyas on every row-3 step, a ladi across row 1, a marigold board; pieces read 94-217 px in the grid where she wants 'product big in frame'. | price and stock 9: all correct, guards per post, P12 deliberately in Crystal; North Star and Petal at 10/10 flagged. | wording truth 8: exemplary words (GREEN not emerald, Toggle clasp never described, Heartbead base metal never named, 'DEMI-FINE · 18K GOLD TONE' true for every card, 'NOT FASHION JEWELLERY. NOT FINE.' is her own line, actual-size cards at 10 px/mm), but relative scale breaks inside frames (P2 soap bar 70 px beside a 500 px bangle; P8 sweets ~20 px beside a 250 px bracelet). | cultural 9: bangle sizes 2.2-2.10, the waning moon still up on Karwa Chauth morning, 'Tai' and 'Bhau' on the money order, a new vessel on Dhanteras, a sugarcane mandap for Tulsi Vivah, Puneri patya; about 15 Marathi strings, all correctly spelt (फॅन्सी, बँक, चष्मा घर, सोन्याची नाणी येथे मिळत नाहीत). | premium vs kitsch 6: symmetrical Deco can be beautiful, but twelve fully drawn shopfronts plus AI steel vessels, toran, baskets, press, camera and a painted backdrop risk a cute storybook. | restraint 5: every cover stacks parapet, board, Devanagari line, pati headline and turn, interior props, piece, plate, steps, pavement and the row device. | captions 8: 'In Pune the shops close from one to four. Ours closed from August to today.', 'from bhau, technically', 'Please don't bite it'; offer line in 4 of 12. | wordmark/type 6: the kit wordmark is used correctly, but 'NAIRA GALLI' is typed in Velista on every cover plate and P1's frame carries the wordmark board + the typed plate + नायरा पेटीट (three NAIRA marks). | originality 9: it alone deliberately avoids every A and B idea-and-piece pair and gives first hero tiles to unsold stock (Kiss Knot, North Star, Fine Tennis, Silk Mesh, Toggle, Petal).
best_posts: P2 BANGLE CENTRE 'NO SOAP. NO SQUEEZE. (it slips over the hand.)': the Kiss Knot's listing fit line as a shared Karwa Chauth memory; 'the glass ones are for the puja. This one is for every day after.' respects the ritual.

P5 BARTAN BHANDAR 'ONE WARM THING ON THE SHELF.' + slide 3 'GOLD COINS NOT SOLD HERE.': the Heartbead's own 'cool and quiet ... only warmth at the front' made visible, and the most honest Dhanteras line in any V3.
P4 POST OFFICE 'BUY SOMETHING NICE.': the money order's amount is the price (₹999), forwardable, 8 days before Bhaubeej.
P7 OPTICIANS 'READ THE LAST LINE.': craft proof (2.5 mm stones, each in its own claw cup) told as an eye test, with an honest '(shown larger.)' loupe.
P1 'BACK AFTER LUNCH. (a long one. eleven weeks.)': owns the silence with the store's real hours on the shutter.
weakest_posts: P12 PHOTO STUDIO: AI painted garden + two umbrellas + three-step riser + three Crystal pieces at 200-260 px; the closing basket is the smallest thing in the frame.
P11 PHOOLWALA: five AI flower baskets, AI sugarcane, AI toran and falling petals around a 13 mm stud on a leaf; densest top-row tile, on a 10/10 variant.
P8 GENERAL STORES: five jars of drawn sweets and a fan around a ~100 px bracelet; repeats the paid 'Almost edible' idea.
P10 WEDDING CARDS: AI letterpress, type cases and a card stand; the Silk Mesh Cuff is the last thing to arrive.
must_fix: Typed sub-brand: 'NAIRA GALLI' is typed in Velista on the plate of all 12 covers, and P1's frame shows the kit wordmark on the board, the typed plate and नायरा पेटीट together. Remove the plate from P1's cover; across P2-P12 either get the owner's yes to 'Naira Galli' as a season name or make the plate read 'गल्ली · N° 02 · SHUTTERS UP' with no NAIRA.

Relative scale inside frames: P2's soap bar (70 x 30) beside a 500 px Kiss Knot and P8's 20 px sweets beside a 250 px Prism make the jewellery read several times life size; scale props to the piece or label 'shown larger.' (the owner rewinds wrong scale).

Density: cut every cover to board + one headline line + piece + plate (move the Cormorant turn into the reel/slide), drop the per-row diyas/torans from covers, and enlarge pieces so each reads at 120 px or more in the grid (P3 hoop 94 px, P8 bracelet ~100 px).

AI props: steel vessels (AI-06/07), toran (AI-09), baskets (AI-11), sugarcane (AI-12), press (AI-10), box camera (AI-13) and the painted backdrop (AI-05) must each pass a reads-AI check at 1080 or fall back to flat SVG; P6's marigold board is the orange she dislikes, test it beside her grid.
Verify the India Security Press, Nashik Road line on P4 before posting (the proposal's fallback is fine); Marathi reader for all ~15 Devanagari strings; Tiro sign-off.
Thin stock: North Star (P4) and Petal Flower Studs (P11) at 10 per metal; re-read the evening before each.
graftable: P5 'GOLD COINS NOT SOLD HERE. / सोन्याची नाणी येथे मिळत नाहीत.' as the Dhanteras honesty line in any option.
P2 'NO SOAP. NO SQUEEZE.' (the Kiss Knot's listing fit) for Karwa Chauth week without the moon.
P4's money order whose amount is the price (₹999 'buy something nice').
P7's eye chart whose last line is the 2.5 mm stones, under a '(shown larger.)' loupe.
P3's actual-size earring cards drawn at 10 px per mm.
P1 'Back after lunch. In Pune the shops close from one to four. Ours closed from August to today.'

scores.criteria: brand fit 9: the one emblem only Naira owns: the real blush drawer box, ported from the site's own CSS box with the owner's tempo (1.1 s out, 1.0 s home, 4 s glint), the kit wordmark on its lid, deck tulips as scenery; packaging is the account's only breakout topic. | owner-taste fit 6: quiet covers and her motion numbers, but the prototype (work/v3box/proto/p2-full.png) shows what the system does to the product: the box fills 60% of the tile and the Ruby bracelet is ~120 px wide (about 43 px in the grid); the aubergine stage floor reads near-black inside the box; P8's 'stage fright' tremble is the jitter she sent back; eleven identical boxes risk sameness. | price and stock 8: all correct with guards, but P2, P9's cover and P12 all lean on Ruby at 12. | wording truth 6: bare 'Emerald' on P2's caption and across P9 (image line 'OUR OWN STYLING NOTE: ONE RUBY AND ONE EMERALD', slot labels, end card, caption, first comment); 'each piece arrives in its own box' unconfirmed for multi-piece orders; otherwise careful (rhodium on Prism, 'Two metals, but only just.', no water claims). | cultural 7: Marathi natak's third bell, प्रयोग on the ticket and the Padwa greeting are right; but the karwa (the puja vessel) is dressed in the bracelet like a mannequin, and P5 casts the piece as 'the understudy' to locker gold. | premium vs kitsch 6: the real box anchors it, but the prototype's karwa reads clip-art and the sets lean craft-fair (crayon forest, cardboard trees, laser-cut elephants, sashed chairs, pop-up heart). | restraint 7: one box, one set, one piece, one ticket per tile; P3's tower is dense. | captions 7: strong hooks ('He will never say the line. On Bhai Dooj he doesn't have to.', 'You were Tree 3.'); offer line in only 3 of 12; 'Emerald' in two. | wordmark/type 9: the wordmark only ever as the lid print, one per frame by construction (P3 hides lower lids, P12 lists shows in type), one Devanagari word all season. | originality 4: the world is new but the content re-treads A and B: P5 is MANGAL's P3 (Woven Gold Hoops + locker + 'Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.'), P4 is MANGAL's Heartbead for Bhai Dooj, P3 is A's Aai/Vahini/friend/you gift guide, P2 is A's late moon, P10 is A's Nocturne for the sangeet, P12 is A and B's Ruby set.
best_posts: P4 'HE WILL NEVER SAY THE LINE. (so the heart says it.)': the struck-out 'Didi, I love y' and the pop-up heart; tender, sendable, the Heartbead's listing line used; posted 8 days early.
P6 'ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT. (this line of light stays on.)': the Fine Tennis Bracelet is 'the everyday line of light' in its own listing; Diwali without diya, marigold or rangoli.
P8 'YOU WERE TREE 3. (annual day. this year, the lead.)': Children's Day spoken to the real buyer, no child shown; the funniest motion idea of the four (once the tremble is calmed).
P1 'PLEASE TAKE YOUR SEATS. (the drawer is the stage.)': the quietest, most on-brand opener: the shut box with a line of light; Prism Rivière, rhodium only, no gold words.
P11 'THE CARD CAME IN A BOX. (so should the gift.)': the box itself as the argument for a size-free wedding gift.
weakest_posts: P5 'THE STAR STAYS IN THE LOCKER.': MANGAL's P3 almost exactly (same piece, same locker, same 'Tuesday gold' line), and 'the understudy' ranks the piece below real gold.
P2 'EVEN THE KARWA DRESSED UP.': a puja vessel used as a mannequin, A's late-moon joke, and in the prototype the hero bracelet is the smallest thing on the tile over a near-black floor.
P9 'THE FRONT ROW SEES IT ALL.': 'EMERALD' printed on the image, end card and caption; four sashed chairs + riser + loupe around two single huggies.
P12 'THE FINALE. CAST OF THREE.': the Ruby set close that A and B both already use, on a variant at 12 selling ~1 a day.
must_fix: Bare 'Emerald': P2 caption 'in Ruby, Crystal or Emerald'; P9 S4 image line, S3 slot labels, S6 end card 'RUBY · CRYSTAL · EMERALD · AMETHYST', caption and first comment. Write 'green' / 'green cubic zirconia' (the brief's rule and the owner's 'green cubic zirconia, not emerald').

Product scale on covers: in the prototype the box takes ~60% of the tile and the piece ~11% of its width. Push in so the drawer stage fills the tile (the proposal's own 'stage view' fallback) or the box, not the jewellery, becomes the hero of eleven tiles.
Night-show paper floors (P2 aubergine #2E2338 tiles) read near-black inside the box at 391x521: lift them to plum or lilac-deep.
P2: dressing the karwa needs the owner's and a native reader's yes; fallback: the bracelet on the parapet beside a plain karwa.
P5 re-treads MANGAL's spine: change the piece and drop 'the understudy' framing (the proposal's own fallback line '(the everyday one goes on every day.)' is better).
P8: replace the 1.6 Hz 'stage fright' tremble with one slow lean; the owner sent back jitter twice.
'Every piece arrives in its own box' (P3, P11, P12): owner confirms multi-piece orders ship one box per piece, else 'every order arrives in the blush Naira box'.
Swap at least two A/B repeats (P3 gift-guide cast, P4 Heartbead for Bhai Dooj, P10 Nocturne for the sangeet, P12 Ruby set); add the exact offer line to the gift posts P4 and P11.
graftable: The real box as an end-card move in any option: the drawer opens at the site's 1.1 s and closes at 1.0 s, lid print as the frame's one wordmark.
P4's struck-through line ('Didi, I love y' → '(hands her a box. says nothing.)') for Bhaubeej.
P6 'ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT. (this line of light stays on.)' for the Fine Tennis Bracelet.
P8 'YOU WERE TREE 3.' as the Children's Day insight.
One Devanagari word (प्रयोग) reused all season, so one native check covers it; the three-bell sound signature.

beats_A_and_B: On the brand-and-truth lens, none of the four clearly beats A. A (Matching Centre, after its fixes) is still the truest feed: Naira's real couture story told literally, one AI texture, one Devanagari line per tile, real photography, the tag fixed in one corner. NAIRA NIWAS comes closest and beats B. It is as true as A on prices, stock and listing words once 'emerald-green' becomes 'green', and it beats A on newness of wit (present-day society life where A uses one institution) and on finale stock safety (the green set, not Ruby). It loses to A on wordmark discipline (typed NAIRA on 11 plates) and on AI exposure (18 plates against A's one). DRAWN FROM LIFE beats both A and B on restraint, premium register and wordmark presence (the kit wordmark on every cover). It loses to both on originality: six of its twelve posts re-run A's or B's jokes and pairings (the late moon, chakli in steel, Prism on a rangoli, 'kisne diya? maine.', A's neckline guide, the Ruby set). It also carries the highest AI-anatomy risk. GALLI beats B on truth and restraint of scripts and matches A on claims hygiene, and it is the most original against both. It loses to A on restraint and premium, because its covers are the densest of any option, and it adds a typed sub-brand. THE BOX THEATRE has the best brand ownership and wordmark rule of all six options, so it beats B on type and marks. It loses to both on product visibility (the prototype's hero bracelet is about 43 px in the grid), on 'Emerald' wording, and on originality: P5 is MANGAL's P3 and P4 is MANGAL's Heartbead Bhai Dooj. Every V3 beats both A and B on motion, which is outside this lens.
recommendation: Brand-and-truth ranking: NAIRA NIWAS 78, DRAWN FROM LIFE 77, NAIRA GALLI 73, THE BOX THEATRE 69. Build NAIRA NIWAS as Variation 3. It is the only one that is new against A and B, truthful in every price, stock and listing word, culturally exact in Marathi, and safe on stock at the top-left tile. Its problems are word and mark fixes, not concept fixes. Before rendering: (1) the kit wordmark replaces the typed 'NAIRA PETITE' and 'NAIRA NIWAS' on fascia, plates and board, and P12's crown carries the wordmark alone, unless the owner says yes to 'Naira Niwas' as a season name; (2) 'emerald-green' becomes 'green' everywhere; (3) 'made to stay gold.' comes off the Dhanteras and Diwali captions and 'LISTED AS TARNISH FREE.' comes off P5's image; (4) every AI prop that sits beside a piece passes a 100% check; (5) the black velvet bed is cropped. Graft into it from DRAWN FROM LIFE: the sign-off 'the moment goes. the piece stays.' on end cards and the 14 px no-line halo. From GALLI: 'GOLD COINS NOT SOLD HERE.' as a P5 slide for Dhanteras honesty, and the optician's '(shown larger.)' loupe. From THE BOX THEATRE: P4's struck-through line device, available for a later Bhaubeej. If the owner wants the most premium, quietest register and accepts re-concepting P2, P3, P6, P9 and the Ruby close so nothing repeats A or B, DRAWN FROM LIFE is the alternative.
